chapterName: Late Republic: Caesar's Civil War and the Ides of March (49-44 BCE)

questions.question: Why was Caesar's reply "I am not Rex, but Caesar" a pun?
options: Caesar was also a Greek word for king
Rex was also a Roman family name
Caesar was the name of a Roman god
Rex was a nickname for Pompey
questions.explanation: Rex meant king but was also a Roman family name, so Caesar joked that the crowd had his name wrong.
questions.sourceQuote: He punned, "I am not Rex, but Caesar," since Rex was also a Roman family name.

questions.question: What did the Rubicon river mark when Caesar crossed it in January 49 BC?
options: The boundary between his province and Italy proper
The edge of Rome's sacred city boundary
The frontier between Italy and Greece
The border between Spain and Gaul
questions.explanation: The small Rubicon separated Caesar's province from Italy proper, so leading troops across it made him a rebel.
questions.sourceQuote: On 10 or 11 January 49 BC, Julius Caesar led his troops across the Rubicon, a small river marking the boundary between his province and Italy proper.

questions.question: Which land had Julius Caesar spent almost ten years conquering by late 50 BC?
options: Spain
Gaul
Britain
Germania
questions.explanation: Caesar had been conquering Gaul, roughly modern France, for almost a decade. By late 50 BC he was rich, famous and backed by devoted legions.
questions.sourceQuote: For almost ten years Julius Caesar had been conquering Gaul, the vast land roughly matching modern France.

questions.question: What did Caesar do when Mark Antony placed a diadem on his head at the Lupercalia?
options: Set it aside, saying Jupiter alone was king
Wore it for the rest of the festival
Threw it into the crowd in anger
Placed it on Pompey's statue instead
questions.explanation: The crowd fell silent at the diadem but cheered when Caesar set it aside. Many suspected he was testing support for a crown.
questions.sourceQuote: Caesar set it aside, declaring that Jupiter alone was king of the Romans, and the crowd cheered.

questions.question: On 1 December 50 BC, what did the Senate vote 370 to 22 in favour of?
options: Pompey taking sole command of Italy
Caesar alone giving up his army
Caesar standing for consul while armed
Both Caesar and Pompey giving up their commands
questions.explanation: The Senate overwhelmingly backed both men laying down their commands. Pompey and a consul rejected the vote anyway.
questions.sourceQuote: On 1 December 50 BC the Senate voted 370 to 22 that both men should lay down their commands, but Pompey and a consul rejected the vote.

questions.question: What did the king of Numidia bring to back the last Pompeian army in North Africa?
options: Some 120 war elephants
A chest of Egyptian gold
Thousands of archers
A fleet of warships
questions.explanation: The Numidian king, ruling roughly modern Algeria, supported the Pompeians with some 120 war elephants.
questions.sourceQuote: A new Pompeian army had gathered in North Africa, backed by the king of Numidia, roughly modern Algeria, with some 120 war elephants.

questions.question: Where did Pompey flee after his defeat at Pharsalus?
options: Pontus
North Africa
Spain
Egypt
questions.explanation: Pompey fled to Egypt, where he was stabbed to death in sight of his wife on the orders of Egypt's boy king.
questions.sourceQuote: After his defeat at Pharsalus, Pompey, once Rome's greatest general, fled to Egypt.

questions.question: How did Cleopatra reach Caesar while he was besieged in Alexandria's palace quarter?
options: She met him on a cruise up the Nile
She slipped secretly into the palace
She was handed over by her brother's regent
She sailed in with his reinforcements
questions.explanation: Cleopatra, feuding with her brother the boy king, secretly entered the palace and became Caesar's lover.
questions.sourceQuote: Cleopatra slipped secretly into the palace and became Caesar's lover.

questions.question: At which battle was Mark Antony defeated in 31 BC?
options: Actium
Munda
Philippi
Pharsalus
questions.explanation: Antony, married to Cleopatra, was beaten at Actium off western Greece, and both took their own lives.
questions.sourceQuote: Antony, who had married Cleopatra, queen of Egypt and Caesar's former lover, was beaten at Actium, off western Greece, in 31 BC, and both took their own lives.

questions.question: According to one ancient biographer, what did Caesar declare when crossing the Rubicon?
options: "The die is cast"
"I am not Rex, but Caesar"
"I came, I saw, I conquered"
"I have hold of you, Africa"
questions.explanation: One ancient biographer reports "the die is cast" (alea iacta est). Another ancient writer says he quoted a Greek poet instead.
questions.sourceQuote: According to one ancient biographer, he declared "the die is cast" (*alea iacta est*).
